text:
erica: Heads-up — NimbusAI asks for a focused perf POC. Main asks: cold-start tail latency (p99/p999), sustain 120 qps with burst to 400 for 60s, and multi-tenant interference check. Also want cost estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted for steady state.

zara: Got it. Do they want embeddings + chat or just text generation?

erica: Chat + retrieval path. 2-step: embed call (short seq) then 2-3 chunked generation calls (seq ~512).

kyle: For cold-starts we should exercise model variants (fp16, 4-bit quantized) and container cold path (no warm KV). Recommend 3 phases: 1) single-node cold boot ramp, 2) sustained 120 qps for 30m, 3) 400 qps 60s bursts, then multi-tenant noise injection.

zara: Agree. Quick plan: Poisson arrival for simmer and burst. Track p50/p95/p99/p999, CPU/GPU utilization, mem pressure, KV cache hit rate, and tail allocator stalls. Also capture token/sec and model-side timeouts.

daniel: For tooling we'll use wrk2 for generation load and a small python client for embed+chat chaining. Sample command for wrk2 (gen-only):

`wrk -t12 -c200 -d180s --rate 120 -s ./scripts/post.lua http://redwood-hosted/prod/v1/generate`

zara: For chain tests run a driver that does: embed -> wait 5ms -> generate with 512 seq. We'll use 1k unique prompts to avoid cache warmup effects.

erica: Security had a Q in the questionnaire: will Dedicated expose customer key material? Nimbus wants KMS integration details and HSM options. That's a gating Enterprise ask.

kyle: We can flag that Dedicated supports KMS + customer-managed keys (bring-your-own) and offer HSM-backed options in Private. I'll draft wording for SSO/KMS section.

zara: Performance notes: Cold-start p999 is sensitive to model shard placement. We'll run 10 cold restarts to get distribution. Also test with background tenant noise at 50% and 100% of baseline QPS.

daniel: Pricing note for Erica — rough ballpark: Hosted: pay-as-you-go token unit + burst credit; Dedicated: reserved GPU pool estimate = $Xk/month for capacity to sustain 120 qps with 20% headroom. I’ll produce a two-line cost delta for the deck.

erica: Nimbus also wants expected degradation modes and automated fallback behavior. Can we demonstrate fallback to a smaller model if tail > SLO?

zara: Yes — include a canary run where model routes to a 70% smaller variant on overload and show latency/cost impact. We'll capture before/after traces.

perf-ci-bot: test-run queued: nimbus-coldstart-1 at 2026-04-10T14:10Z

kyle: Ops/infra checklist: reserve one Dedicated node in staging AZ, ensure telemetry (prom/pushgateway) has 10s scrape, enable kv-prefix caching disabled for first phase. Also enable perf profiler for a 2m window around bursts.

erica: Timeline: kickoff tomorrow, run quick smoke (10m) then full run day-after. Can we have a one-page results summary within 24h of run end? Nimbus expects quick turnaround.

zara: Yes. I’ll capture a short summary + 1 figure (p999 CDF) + 1 table (throughput vs p99) and attach to the demo.

daniel: Action items: (1) kyle reserve node + toggle KV cache (2) zara build driver and test scripts (3) daniel draft cost numbers and KMS text (4) erica share prospect context + security contact.

erica: Thanks — I’ll loop in their infra lead and post the questionnaire contact. :thumbsup:

kyle: Quick note on measurement: include cold-start wallclock (time from request accepted to first token) and model-internal time from server logs. People often confuse them.

zara: Also add a deterministic noise run: pin background tenant to repeatable synthetic workload so we can compare apples-to-apples across model builds.

perf-ci-bot: test-run started: nimbus-coldstart-1 (phase 1) at 2026-04-10T14:22Z

erica: Perfect. I’ll update Nimbus and schedule the handoff call after the smoke completes.

kyle: If we see >2x p999 on cold restarts we’ll snapshot logs and open a follow-up with infra team.

zara: Will do. I’ll post the first run results in this thread when available.

erica: Awesome — appreciate the quick turnaround team.
